item.title: Contextual Optimization with Side Information: Theory, Methodology, and Applications
item.content:encoded:
Stelios Bekiros, University of Turin

Andrea D'Ariano, Roma Tre University

Peng Wu, Fuzhou University

Guowei Zhang, Dalian University of Technology

Modern operations research integrates optimization with machine learning and statistics to incorporate side information—such as demand patterns and market conditions—into decision-making processes. This contextual optimization approach enables more adaptive and data-driven policies than classical optimization, though significant challenges persist including high-dimensional data, noisy observations, distribution shifts, and computational constraints.

The field requires new theories and frameworks that systematically combine learning and optimization under uncertainty, with emphasis on improving actual operational performance. This special issue invites high-quality contributions developing novel theories, models, algorithms, and applications addressing contextual decision-making using side information, spanning prescriptive analytics, adaptive algorithms, and real-world applications in transportation, supply chains, and healthcare.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
